# Test plan

*Generated by `homelab testplan` — regenerate after adding a suite.*

Phase 7 asks for a document describing every suite and every accepted
limitation. This one is derived from the tests rather than written beside
them, because a file a person keeps in step with reality drifts out of it
(Kenny, 2026-09-02). What each suite is FOR comes from its own header;
what it checks comes from the test names, which in this codebase are
sentences. A test that is deleted disappears from here in the same commit.

**407 tests across 23 suites.**

## Accepted limitations

Gaps somebody looked at and decided to leave, with the reason. Lifted
from the gap table in `REALIZATION_PLAN.md` so the two cannot disagree.

- **G6** — the 325-line fact-gatherer feeding every nightly finding has no test · _**later** (Kenny: closing it means rebuilding it to take an executor)_

## Suites

### `core/tests/busy_tests.rs`

O10: the check that keeps an update out of somebody's evening.

- `o10_a_paused_film_still_counts_as_busy` — The real answer when somebody has a film open and paused.
- `o10_open_but_idle_sessions_do_not_block` — Sessions open but nothing playing: an idle browser tab is not an evening.
- `o10_nobody_connected_allows_the_update`
- `o10_every_uncertain_answer_blocks_the_update` — The heart of it.
- `o10_the_v1_field_is_not_what_decides` — A field that does not exist cannot be a test.

### `core/tests/checks_tests.rs`

J1-J3: the before/after pair, and why there are no thresholds in it.

Covers: F156

- `j1_a_count_may_rise_and_must_not_fall` — Kenny's objection, as a test.
- `j1_the_pair_needs_no_tolerance_because_it_is_taken_minutes_apart` — The media rebuild is the case: the downloader was importing throughout, so "equal" would have failed a healthy rebuild and "at least N" would have been a guess about a library that changes hourly.
- `must_match_catches_a_changed_setting` — Configuration is not content: a library path or a transcoding device that changed is a fault even though nothing got smaller.
- `an_unreadable_measurement_is_not_a_regression` — A command that will not run says nothing about the data.
- `a_first_deploy_has_nothing_to_compare_and_passes` — A fresh container has no before.
- `blind_spots_are_reported_with_a_green_result` — The blind spots come back even when everything passed, because that is exactly the moment nobody asks what was not checked.
- `a_service_whose_deepest_check_is_a_port_is_refused` — Kenny's challenge, as a rule rather than an intention.
- `a_shallow_check_must_declare_its_blind_spot` — And a shallow check must say what it does not prove, because that is exactly the one that gets mistaken for proof.
- `a_service_without_checks_is_not_nagged` — A service with no checks at all is not judged.
- `a_question_nobody_answers_never_reads_as_permission` — The answer that matters most is the one nobody gives.
- `a_deliberate_drop_can_be_allowed_but_never_by_silence` — T69, the half that matters: the mechanism is actually wired to the case Kenny named.

### `core/tests/deploy_tests.rs`

The M0 safety and idempotency suite — every scenario here maps to a FEATURES.md test scenario (A1, A2, A3/D10, B1, D1, A5).

Covers: F107, F124, F129, F130, F133, F137, F141, F143, F144, F145, F146, F147, F159, F164, F169, F170, F173, F21, F210, F213, F22

- `a_clone_refuses_a_privilege_level_the_template_cannot_give` — A clone can never change a container's privilege level, so asking for one the template cannot give must stop the deploy rather than silently produce the other.
- `a_privileged_stack_cloning_the_privileged_template_is_allowed` — And the matching case passes: a privileged stack cloning the privileged template is exactly how the media and downloader stacks are built.
- `o7_config_paths_must_be_named_after_their_app` — O7: a config path must be named `<app>-config`.
- `a_mount_inside_a_read_only_mount_is_refused` — A bind mount inside a READ-ONLY bind mount of the same service is refused; inside a writable one it is fine.
- `o5_host_owner_uid_must_match_the_privilege_level` — O5: on an unprivileged container uid 1000 inside is uid 101000 on the host, so the two privilege levels need host_owner_uid values 100000 apart.
- `a1_no_touch_vmid_is_refused_with_zero_commands`
- `a2_hostname_mismatch_refuses_reuse`
- `d10_path_traversal_is_refused_before_any_command`
- `d10_validator_collects_all_problems`
- `a_bind_inside_a_declared_mount_is_covered_by_it` — A bind INSIDE a declared mount is covered by it.
- `a_deploy_installs_the_unit_file_and_starts_a_service_that_is_down` — Kenny's N1 (2026-08-31): the unit file lives in the repository and a deploy puts it there.
- `a_running_native_service_is_never_restarted_by_a_deploy` — A service that is already running is left running.
- `a_declared_unit_without_its_file_is_refused` — A declared unit with no unit file is refused, loudly.
- `native_only_lets_a_container_declare_that_it_runs_no_docker` — Kenny asked the right question on 2026-08-31: the four native services could be backed up and updated, but nothing in the repository said how to rebuild the container they run on.
- `a_native_only_container_is_never_given_docker` — Such a container must never be given docker: installing it would change the very thing the manifest exists to reproduce.
- `m1_a_borrowed_directory_is_mounted_but_never_created` — The media libraries are two ZFS datasets that Proxmox hands to the fileserver and to the media container at the same time.
- `m1_a_missing_borrowed_directory_stops_the_deploy` — A missing one is refused.
- `m1_the_two_kinds_of_directory_cannot_be_confused` — The two lists stay distinct, in both directions.
- `m1_a_stack_without_borrowed_directories_is_never_probed` — A stack with no borrowed directories must not be asked about any.
- `a_missing_mount_is_reattached_on_an_existing_container` — A mount that is missing from a live container is put back by a deploy.
- `protection_is_put_back_when_the_stack_file_asks_for_it` — The protection flag is intent like any other, and it was only ever set on the run that created the container.
- `matching_mounts_are_left_completely_alone` — A container whose mounts already match is not written to at all, and its protection flag is never touched.
- `w3_a_deploy_puts_a_drifted_boot_policy_back` — The W3 acceptance criterion's second half: a boot order moved by hand is corrected by a deploy.
- `w3_a_container_that_agrees_is_not_written_to` — A container that already agrees is left alone — the check must not produce a write on every deploy.
- `w1_a_gpu_stack_is_refused_when_the_host_has_no_card` — F54, the most self-concealing failure left in the fleet: a stack with `gpu: true` on a host with no card comes up perfectly and transcodes on the CPU.
- `w1_the_device_group_ids_are_read_from_the_host` — The other half of F54: the group ids were the literals 44 and 104, right on this host and silently wrong on any other.
- `w1_a_vpn_stack_is_refused_when_the_host_has_no_tun` — The same shape for the VPN flag: without /dev/net/tun the container starts and only the tunnel inside it fails, where nothing is looking.
- `w1_a_stack_without_hardware_is_never_probed` — A stack that asks for no hardware must not be probed at all — a check that runs where it has no business is a check that can refuse a deploy for a reason that does not apply to it.
- `m7_a_replaced_stack_recovers_its_backup_time_from_the_repository` — A C4 replacement destroys the container and its state record together, so "preserve the previous value" preserves nothing.
- `a_deploy_never_unregisters_the_native_services_on_its_stack` — The native services registered on a stack are not the deploy's to forget.
- `m7_a_stack_with_no_snapshots_records_zero_and_still_deploys` — The other direction, which is what makes the test above mean anything: a stack whose repository has nothing to say still records a zero, and the deploy still succeeds.
- `m7_a_plain_redeploy_keeps_its_record_without_asking_restic` — A redeploy over a container that still exists keeps the value it already had, and must not spend a restic round trip finding that out.
- `e3_auto_restore_reads_the_configured_repository` — The repository that deploy reads must be the one the host is configured with.
- `d1_fresh_deploy_command_sequence`
- `t52_a_changed_config_file_restarts_its_app` — T52: pushing a config file is not the same as the service reading it.
- `t52_a_changed_compose_file_does_not_restart_twice` — The other half: when only the compose file changed, `up -d` recreates the container by itself and a restart on top of that is pure churn.
- `t56_a_private_registry_is_signed_into_before_the_pull` — T56: an image behind a login must not need a step nobody wrote down.
- `t56_a_stack_without_a_registry_never_logs_in` — A stack with no private registry must not gain a login step it never asked for.
- `b1_second_run_is_quiet`
- `a5_env_goes_to_vault_never_to_repo`
- `h1_gateway_route_only_to_the_gateway`
- `f129_a_cache_that_cannot_serve_falls_back_to_the_real_registry` — F129 · the fallback half of C1: a cache that answers its probe but cannot serve a blob must not be able to hold the deploy hostage.
- `s2_a_failed_redeploy_marks_the_step_without_rewriting_what_applied` — S2b · a stack ALREADY on record whose redeploy stops half-way.
- `s2_a_failed_deploy_still_records_the_stack` — S2a · a deploy that stops half-way must still leave a record.
- `s2_a_refused_target_records_nothing_at_all` — S2a-bis · but a refusal is not a half-deploy.
- `s2_reconcile_catches_a_container_that_does_not_match` — S2b · the reconciliation pass rejects a deploy whose steps all succeeded but whose container does not match the stack file.
- `s2_a_push_that_did_not_land_fails_its_own_step` — S2c · a push that reports success and did not land fails its own step, not three steps later.
- `storage_the_app_cannot_write_fails_the_deploy` — Can the application write its own data? That, and nothing about uids.
- `storage_the_app_can_write_says_nothing` — And it must stay quiet when the app CAN write, whatever the uids happen to be — the half that decides whether a check survives a month.
- `storage_a_directory_the_app_does_not_mount_is_skipped` — A directory the app does not mount is not its business.
- `h4_cadvisor_is_installed_by_the_guards_on_every_docker_host` — H4 · cAdvisor is installed on every managed docker host, not declared per stack.
- `h4_cadvisor_is_started_even_when_its_compose_file_is_unchanged` — And it must bring cadvisor up even when the compose file is ALREADY there.
- `h4_cadvisor_is_not_installed_where_there_is_no_docker` — And never on a container that runs no docker: a weekly prune timer on a native-only host has been failing every week since it was installed, which is worse than useless — a guard that fails on schedule teaches you to ignore failures.
- `a_staging_path_is_unique_per_target_file` — T74: two files bound for two different containers must not share a staging path on the host.
- `a_path_declared_reproducible_gets_no_repository` — A path declared reproducible gets no restic repository at all.
- `switching_a_backup_off_requires_saying_why` — The flag cannot be set without a reason a person can still read later.
- `a_declared_path_that_is_not_there_yet_says_deploy_first` — Z5: a declared path that is not on disk yet gets a message that names the real problem.
- `a_vmid_that_is_a_qemu_vm_is_refused_even_when_it_is_not_on_the_list` — covers: F210  Every existing test mocks `qm status` as FAILED, so this branch — the one that refuses to touch a QEMU VM at all — had never been executed.
- `a_route_filename_may_not_climb_out_of_the_routes_directory` — covers: F210  The path-traversal guard on the ONE sanctioned cross-stack write.
- `the_update_labels_the_code_reads_exist_somewhere_in_the_fleet` — covers: F213  G2 of the Phase-7 gate.
- `compose_files`
- `a_deploy_registers_the_questions_only_a_person_can_answer` — G17 · a deploy that prints a manual check must also register it.
- `the_missing_account_is_created_before_anything_starts`
- `a_unit_whose_program_is_absent_is_not_started_and_the_reason_is_named`
- `a_missing_env_file_is_restored_from_the_vault_rather_than_invented`
- `a_secret_that_exists_nowhere_stops_the_start_instead_of_looping`

### `core/tests/devicebackup_tests.rs`

Route A (Kenny, form J1 via the OPNsense session, 2026-09-02): the orchestrator asks a device it may not touch for its own configuration and stores the answer in restic.

Covers: F205

- `the_credential_never_reaches_the_command_line` — covers: F205  The credential must never reach argv: `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is world-readable, and this one can download a router's entire configuration.
- `a_snapshot_too_small_to_be_a_configuration_fails` — covers: F205  A login page is a 200 with a body, and restic stores whatever it is handed.
- `an_unverified_certificate_is_used_but_never_quietly` — covers: F205  Verification is configuration-dependent (rule 24), so the code cannot enforce it — but it must not be silent about running without it.
- `a_pinned_public_key_is_what_verifies_the_connection` — covers: F205  The pin is what verifies this connection, and it must reach curl exactly.

### `core/tests/failure_model_tests.rs`

M1 failure-model suite (AR13, AR14, AR16, F6). Every scenario maps to a FEATURES.md / ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md test scenario.

- `ar14_failed_deploy_writes_replayable_bundle`
- `ar16_commands_script_extracts_only_run_lines`
- `ar13_interrupted_op_detected_from_journal`
- `ar13_completed_op_is_not_flagged`
- `f6_doctor_healthy_system_is_ok`
- `f6_doctor_flags_each_problem_with_remedy`
- `recording_sink_tees_and_records`

### `core/tests/fleetcheck_tests.rs`

Y4: the fleet check has one job — find the things that look healthy.

Covers: F149, F184, F198, F211, F214, F79

- `y4_a_healthy_fleet_is_silent` — A healthy fleet produces nothing.
- `y4_finds_the_kyu_case` — The kyu case, exactly: the record still describes the pre-rename hostname, so every operation fails the guard, the nightly run failed, H8 disabled the stack, and it had never been backed up.
- `y4_finds_a_vanished_container` — A container removed outside the orchestrator leaves a record pointing at nothing.
- `y4_finds_a_stack_file_aimed_at_someone_elses_container` — The stacks/cloudflared case: a file claiming vmid 109, which was kyu.
- `y4_finds_routes_that_lead_nowhere` — Both dead routes: the one to the empty MQTT container and the one to Kenny's own workstation.
- `y4_finds_a_backup_that_quietly_stopped` — A backup that stopped is not visible from the outside — the files are still there, they are just old.
- `y4_probe_address_covers_every_route_shape_in_the_house` — The probe address, which the first live run got wrong twice.
- `healthy_container_reports_no_growth_findings` — The baseline that makes the rest meaningful: a container inside every limit produces nothing at all.
- `missing_guards_are_reported` — CT 104's shape before the rollout: guards written months earlier that had never run there.
- `docker_logs_and_journal_are_checked_separately` — Loki's 923 MB lived in docker's log directory, not the journal.
- `a_nearly_full_disk_is_broken_not_drift` — A full rootfs is the one growth case that is not merely drift: from here an image pull or an apt upgrade can fail halfway.
- `swap_in_use_is_reported` — CT 106 sat at 1028 MB of swap, which is what prompted G2.
- `limits_are_honoured_rather_than_hardcoded` — The limits are configurable (standing rule 27), so a fleet with different tolerances gets different answers from the same facts.
- `every_container_is_reported_independently` — The check runs over the whole fleet, and one loud container must not mask the others.
- `a_stack_with_no_prometheus_target_is_reported` — A stack nobody is scraping is a stack whose failure nobody will see.
- `a_dashboard_grafana_never_received_is_reported` — The deploy writing a dashboard is not the same question as Grafana having it, and for seven weeks only the first was asked.
- `an_unasked_dashboard_question_is_never_a_finding` — And the unasked question must stay unasked.
- `a_stack_whose_logs_never_arrive_is_reported` — Logs that go nowhere look exactly like a quiet service — which is why the window this is asked over is a setting and not the hour it started as.
- `an_unasked_question_is_never_a_finding` — The rule that keeps this check believable: a question that was not asked must never become a finding.
- `a_covered_stack_is_silent` — A fully covered stack says nothing at all.
- `w3_a_hand_edited_boot_order_is_reported` — The W3 acceptance criterion, first half: a container whose boot order was moved by hand is reported.
- `w3_resources_are_reported_with_the_remedy_that_applies` — Resources diverge with a different remedy, because a deploy deliberately does not change them under a running service.
- `w3_a_container_that_matches_says_nothing` — Agreement is silence, and an unasked question is not a finding: a stack whose record carries no manifest is skipped rather than guessed at.
- `w3_the_repair_touches_boot_policy_and_nothing_else` — The repair side stays as narrow as the reporting side is wide: the arguments a deploy would apply cover boot policy only, never resources.
- `a_swapping_container_on_a_short_host_is_not_told_to_take_more_memory` — F184: a remedy that cannot be carried out is not a remedy.
- `a_watched_backup_that_stopped_is_a_finding` — covers: F198  A backup this suite does not make but does watch.
- `a_stack_that_clones_a_template_which_is_gone_is_a_finding` — covers: F211  A stack whose golden template no longer exists on the hypervisor.
- `a_stack_that_deliberately_keeps_nothing_is_noted_not_broken` — covers: F211  The branch that decides whether "never been backed up" is a fault or a decision.
- `a_deliberate_decision_never_raises_the_alarm_but_is_never_hidden_either` — covers: F214  G15 of the Phase-7 gate, the testable half.
- `a_finished_deploy_says_nothing`
- `a_deploy_that_stopped_halfway_is_reported_with_the_step_it_stopped_at`
- `the_full_round_carries_it_so_the_nightly_report_does_too`
- `the_full_round_carries_the_manual_checks` — G17: the unanswered question has to ride the round that already reaches Kenny, or it is a record nobody reads — the fault this whole audit is about.
- `only_a_2xx_counts_as_delivered`
- `the_fallback_is_tried_after_the_primary_and_never_twice`
- `a_working_notification_path_is_not_a_finding`
- `a_notification_that_reached_no_route_is_reported_with_what_it_said`
- `a_path_that_never_worked_says_that_rather_than_a_misleading_zero`
- `the_full_round_carries_it`
- `the_full_round_carries_the_restore_drill` — G14: the drill's verdict has to ride the round that already reaches Kenny.
- `a_recent_run_with_nothing_stale_says_nothing`
- `a_monitor_for_a_stack_that_is_gone_is_named` — The case Kenny found by noticing ping errors on a Grafana panel: a drill container destroyed hours earlier, still pinged every minute.
- `a_seeder_that_stopped_running_is_broken_not_quiet`
- `one_that_has_never_run_says_so_rather_than_looking_healthy`
- `a_run_that_judged_nothing_does_not_read_as_all_clear` — F175's lesson, kept: without a list to compare against, "nothing stale" is not an all-clear.
- `an_unreadable_status_file_is_a_finding_not_a_silence`
- `the_full_round_carries_it`

### `core/tests/homepage_tests.rs`

T51: the front page rendered from the routes the orchestrator already writes, instead of a file somebody maintains.

Covers: F166, F188, F190, F195, F197, F200

- `a_route_fragment_yields_its_hostnames_and_its_backends` — covers: F166
- `a_stack_without_routes_is_skipped_rather_than_rendered_empty`
- `rendering_twice_produces_the_same_bytes`
- `a_generated_file_takes_the_owner_of_the_directory_it_lands_in` — covers: F190  A generated file lands in a directory that belongs to a CONTAINER, and the orchestrator writes it as host root.
- `a_failing_chown_does_not_fail_the_write` — The chown is best-effort: a convenience file must never fail a deploy.
- `the_overlay_supplies_what_a_route_cannot_and_nothing_else` — covers: F188  The real overlay, verbatim from the repo, joined with routes shaped like the ones the gateway actually holds.
- `merging_twice_produces_the_same_bytes` — Same input, same bytes — a deploy that changes nothing must report "unchanged" rather than rewrite the file every night.
- `a_widget_is_derived_from_the_route_and_the_application` — covers: F195  Kenny asked whether the live tiles — what is streaming, how many films — could be automatic.
- `a_missing_key_still_produces_a_widget` — A key that cannot be read must fail visibly rather than vanish: the tile still gets a widget, pointing at Homepage's own variable, so Homepage reports the problem instead of the widget quietly not being there.
- `a_second_route_to_the_same_door_is_not_a_second_tile` — covers: F195  Not every route is a front door.
- `overlay_lines_sit_under_their_service_not_beside_it` — covers: F197  The bug this catches shipped once and no test saw it: every assertion asked whether a line was PRESENT, not where it sat.
- `tiles_follow_the_order_written_in_the_overlay` — covers: F197  Media is first because Kenny asked for it, and within Media Jellyfin is first for the same reason.
- `the_generated_page_is_valid_yaml` — covers: F200  The test that should have existed from the first line of this generator.

### `core/tests/logshipper_tests.rs`

C1/C2 · the replacement for a log shipper that reached end of life.

- `every_label_promtail_set_is_still_set` — The labels are the contract.
- `the_container_name_is_read_from_tag_and_not_from_name` — F72, pinned: docker puts the container's name in `attrs.tag`, and reading `attrs.name` instead is what left three dashboards empty for months.
- `the_journal_is_read_because_on_a_native_container_that_is_the_log` — The half promtail never had on these containers.
- `it_points_at_the_loki_it_was_given_and_nowhere_else`
- `installing_is_idempotent_and_says_so_without_doing_anything` — A deploy runs this every time.
- `the_package_comes_from_a_signed_repository` — The apt route is the point: it is what keeps the shipper patched, which is the whole reason for leaving promtail behind.
- `alloy_is_given_read_access_to_all_three_sources` — A shipper that cannot read the files it is pointed at delivers nothing and reports itself healthy — the fault this whole migration exists to escape.
- `the_config_goes_where_the_packaged_unit_already_looks`
- `the_base_address_becomes_the_push_endpoint`
- `an_address_that_already_names_the_path_is_left_alone`
- `the_generated_config_carries_the_push_path_and_not_the_base`
- `dropped_bytes_mean_the_far_end_refused_them` — The exact state the first live deploy was in while reporting success.
- `sent_bytes_with_none_dropped_is_the_only_good_answer`
- `nothing_either_way_is_reported_as_nothing_either_way` — Nothing sent and nothing dropped is genuinely ambiguous, and saying so beats picking the flattering reading.
- `no_answer_is_not_a_healthy_answer`
- `dropping_outranks_sending` — Dropping wins over sending: a shipper that delivered something and then started losing batches is broken, not fine.
- `several_endpoints_are_summed_rather_than_the_first_one_taken`
- `the_journal_job_label_is_forced_and_not_left_to_alloy` — Alloy names a job after the component that produced it, so the journal arrived as `job="loki.source.journal.journal"` on the first live run.

### `core/tests/m4_ops_tests.rs`

M4 operation tests: gated destroy (C2) and backup/restore (E1/E2).

Covers: F105, F153, F154, F156, F162, F180, F207, F209, F210, F36, F75

- `c2_destroy_refuses_wrong_typed_name`
- `c2_destroy_refuses_no_touch_vmid`
- `c2_destroy_refuses_hostname_mismatch`
- `c2_destroy_happy_path_lifts_protection_then_destroys`
- `c2_destroy_removes_the_dashboard_on_the_gateway_not_the_host` — The dashboard a destroy removes lives on the GATEWAY, so the removal has to happen there.
- `e1_backup_runs_init_quiesce_snapshot_resume_retention`
- `w2_a_stack_keeps_snapshots_by_its_own_policy` — W2's acceptance criterion: two stacks with different retention produce demonstrably different forget decisions.
- `e1_backup_resumes_every_container_it_paused_even_one_not_in_apps` — The backup must resume exactly what it paused, not what the manifest happens to list.
- `e1_backup_with_nothing_to_pause_starts_nothing` — Nothing labelled means nothing stopped and nothing to start back — the step must not invent a bare `docker start` with no arguments.
- `every_stack_dashboard_has_an_errors_section` — Every stack dashboard carries its own errors-only section, because Kenny asked for it on every one rather than only on the fleet-wide page — and because a stack deployed next month must get it without anyone remembering to add it.
- `a_path_declared_empty_is_not_backed_up_and_must_really_be_empty` — A restic run over a directory that exists and is empty succeeds, writes a snapshot with nothing in it, and reports success.
- `every_restic_call_names_a_cache_directory` — Every restic invocation must name a cache directory.
- `a_snapshot_that_stored_nothing_is_recognised` — covers: F105
- `e2_restore_validates_quiesces_restores_resumes_verifies`
- `e2_restore_fails_when_app_not_running_after`
- `d9_update_capture_pull_verify_order`
- `d9_auto_update_skips_non_auto_policy`

- `t2_deploy_provisions_a_dashboard_for_the_stack` — T2: a stack brings its own dashboard.
- `t2_the_generated_dashboard_is_scoped_and_stable` — The generated document has to be worth provisioning: real panels, the Prometheus datasource by uid, and every query scoped to this stack so two stacks never show each other's numbers.
- `t1_discovery_is_off_when_unconfigured` — T1: with no directory configured the feature is simply off, and a deploy neither writes nor complains.
- `d25_backup_writes_one_repo_per_owning_app` — D25: one restic repository per APP, not per stack.
- `o5_clone_refuses_a_privilege_level_the_template_cannot_give` — O5: `pct clone` takes no `--unprivileged`, so a clone always inherits the template's privilege level.
- `f38_restore_honours_the_configured_timeout` — F38: the restore timeout was a hardcoded 1800 s while the backup side had already been raised to four hours for exactly the same reason — a first multi-GB transfer over a residential uplink.
- `o6_restore_is_per_path_not_per_stack` — O6: the auto-restore used to be all-or-nothing — it only ran when EVERY path in `storage:` was empty.
- `e3_env_restored_from_vault_when_client_sends_none`
- `d3_removed_app_is_stopped_and_deleted_but_config_kept`
- `h6_appdata_routes_dir_written_host_side`

- `h7_newer_schema_refused_missing_file_is_fresh`

- `h14_failed_step_leaves_running_then_failed_trail`

- `a_destroy_backs_the_stack_up_before_it_removes_anything` — Kenny asked whether a destroy takes a backup first.
- `a_failed_backup_stops_the_destroy` — And when that backup fails, nothing is destroyed.
- `t66_destroy_removes_the_dashboard_the_deploy_wrote` — T66 · whatever a deploy registers, a destroy has to unregister.
- `t69_a_regressed_check_fails_the_deploy_when_nobody_is_watching` — A reading that fell, with nobody watching: the deploy fails.

- `e2_an_unknown_snapshot_id_is_refused_before_anything_is_stopped` — covers: F207  G5.

- `a_destroy_that_takes_no_backup_always_says_why` — covers: F210  G11 of the Phase-7 gate, third part.

### `core/tests/native_tests.rs`

C7: native-service adoption. The refusals carry the feature: adopting a container that is not what the manifest claims would point every later backup and update at the wrong thing.

Covers: F117, F171

- `c7_validation_catches_the_lies`
- `c7_adopt_records_state_without_touching_the_service`
- `c7_adopt_refuses_inactive_unit`
- `c7_adopt_refuses_unit_running_a_different_binary`
- `c7_adopt_refuses_no_touch_and_wrong_hostname`
- `c7_adopt_refuses_repointing_an_existing_stack`
- `c7_native_backup_streams_tar_into_restic`
- `c7_supervised_update_restarts_only_on_binary_change`
- `c7_supervised_update_rolls_back_when_new_version_stays_down`
- `t5_a_stack_holds_several_native_services` — T5: several native services share one container — the layout puts kyu, kyu-runner and http-switchboard on CT 109.
- `t5_pre_list_state_migrates_on_load` — T5 migration: state written before native services became a list still loads, and its single service moves into the list.
- `d25_native_backup_uses_the_service_name_for_its_repo` — D25 for native services: the repository is named after the SERVICE, not the stack.
- `c7_adoption_tags_the_container_as_managed` — The `homelab` tag is what makes "managed" visible in the Proxmox list, and it was only ever applied where a container is created.
- `c7_adoption_never_clobbers_existing_tags` — A container that already carries the tag is not written to again, and a container that carries somebody else's tags keeps them.
- `an_install_refuses_a_unit_file_that_runs_a_different_binary` — A unit file that runs a different program than the manifest declares is refused BEFORE anything is written.
- `an_install_without_a_unit_file_is_refused` — An empty unit file is its own refusal.
- `an_install_stages_beside_the_target_before_it_replaces_anything` — The happy path: stage beside the target, install the unit, activate, and end up recorded in state exactly as adoption would record it — a service built this way and one taken over by hand must be indistinguishable afterwards.
- `a_first_install_that_fails_says_there_is_nothing_to_roll_back_to` — A FIRST install that does not come up has nothing to roll back to, and the message has to say so.
- `a_reinstall_that_fails_returns_to_the_binary_that_was_running` — A RE-install that does not come up returns to the binary that was running.
- `a_release_source_that_is_half_declared_is_refused` — The release source is part of the stack file or it is nowhere.
- `the_native_backup_uses_the_same_restic_cache_as_every_other` — F171: the native backup builds its restic environment by hand, and the hand-built copy had drifted from the one every compose stack gets.

### `core/tests/register_tests.rs`

The register claims, the tests prove — and until now nothing held the two together.

- `every_covers_marker_names_a_real_finding` — Rule 1: a marker that names a finding the register does not have.
- `every_claimed_test_exists_and_names_its_finding` — Rule 2: a row that claims a test must name one that exists and that says so itself.
- `a_claimed_test_belongs_to_a_closed_finding` — And the claim has to be worth making: a row that names a test must be one that was actually closed.
- `no_finding_recorded_since_the_rule_may_claim_done_without_naming_its_proof`
- `no_finding_at_all_claims_done_while_pointing_at_nothing` — The backlog is worked off, so this now holds the ground rather than measuring the descent.

### `core/tests/registry_cache_tests.rs`

D60: the image rewrite that points a pull at the cache in the house.

- `an_image_reference_is_split_the_way_docker_splits_it` — Docker's naming rules are not obvious, and getting them wrong produces a 404 from the cache rather than an error anyone can read.
- `every_image_is_pointed_at_the_cache_when_it_answers`
- `an_upstream_that_did_not_answer_is_left_alone` — The whole reason Kenny chose this variant: a cache that does not answer costs speed, not the deploy.
- `a_private_registry_is_never_routed_through_the_cache` — The cache is anonymous, so a private image must keep going to its own registry with its own token.
- `only_image_lines_are_rewritten` — Lines that are not an image reference are never touched — including a comment that happens to mention one.
- `the_daemon_config_declares_the_cache_addresses` — The daemon has to be told the cache speaks plain HTTP, or every cached pull fails with "server gave HTTP response to HTTPS client" — which reads like a broken cache rather than a missing setting.

G14 · the recurring restore drill, and the rule that a drill which can be satisfied by empty files rehearses nothing.

- `a_drill_that_has_never_run_is_always_due`
- `a_passed_drill_counts_for_the_configured_window_and_not_a_day_longer`
- `the_turn_goes_round_so_a_year_covers_every_repository`

- `a_recent_passing_drill_is_not_a_finding`

### `core/tests/secrets_tests.rs`

Standing rule 10: secrets never in git, argv, logs, state or transcripts — and these tests ASSERT it. A deploy runs with a planted secret; every observable surface is scanned for the plaintext.

Covers: F206

- `r10_secret_never_in_transcript_events`
- `r10_secret_never_in_argv`
- `r10_secret_only_in_vault_and_push_tmp_never_in_repo_or_state`

### `core/tests/stack_files_tests.rs`

G10 · the thirteen stack files that actually run this house, validated.

- `every_stack_file_on_disk_passes_the_validator_a_deploy_would_run`

- `every_promtail_label_names_the_container_it_actually_runs_on` — Found by making this mistake while building the drill stack: a `sed` over a copied config left `host: 117-app-drill` on a container called `118-app-drill`.

- `every_stack_without_an_application_monitor_is_one_we_named` — A stack with no monitor at all is not automatically wrong — the mechanical half already pings every container.

- `the_runbook_names_the_repositories_restic_actually_uses` — The runbook must name the repositories restic actually writes to.

- `the_recyclarr_preset_keeps_its_two_deliberate_absences` — T7: the Recyclarr configuration carries two absences that are DECISIONS, and both of them look like something a helpful hand would fill in.
- `every_stack_manifest_agrees_with_the_directories_beside_it` — T49: a stack file and the directories beside it have to agree.
- `every_native_service_in_the_repository_is_found_with_its_unit_file` — The two shapes a native stack takes on this fleet are both read.
- `a_native_stack_gets_the_native_operation_from_the_same_key` — A native stack must not be sent a compose operation.
- `a_waiting_step_is_answerable_from_the_window_the_operator_is_reading` — T69: a waiting step reaches the operator where they are already looking, and both keys say what they do.
- `every_cli_verb_appears_in_the_usage_text` — covers: F212  G20 of the Phase-7 gate.
- `every_app_either_has_checks_or_is_named_as_deliberately_without` — covers: F215  G18 of the Phase-7 gate.
- `the_committed_test_plan_matches_a_fresh_generation` — The generated test plan must match what the tests actually say, for the same reason the runbook must: a document nobody regenerates is a document that describes last month.
- `the_help_text_and_the_usage_message_agree_about_install_native` — The help text and the usage message must describe the same command.
